analysis.title: Living on the Edge: The Rise of Distributed Power
key_insights: Morgan Stanley argues AI infrastructure is hitting a physical limit. The grid cannot deliver power fast enough, inference suits smaller nodes closer to users, and political resistance is making 1 GW+ mega-campus data centers harder to build. The result is a structural shift to distributed behind-the-meter (BTM) power.

Time-to-power is becoming as important as cost-of-power. MS introduces the Stranded Compute Adjusted Cost of Power (SCACP), which adds the cost of idle GPUs to the conventional levelized cost of electricity (LCOE). Every year of expedited power access is valued at about $42/MWh over a 15-year project life.

Power shortfall math: 160 GW of incremental US data center power demand in 2026-2029, less 22 GW under construction with a grid connection, 36 GW of available grid capacity, 23 GW of BTM equipment already procured, and probability-weighted nuclear siting. That leaves a 77 GW shortfall to be filled by BTM generation.
MS forecasts a ~120 GW, or $240bn, BTM power equipment TAM through 2029, made up of 77 GW for data centers and 40 GW for commercial and industrial (C&I) customers.

Composite BTM ranking today: Bloom Energy's solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) is #1 (4.5/5, SCACP $131/MWh), BorgWarner's micro turbine generator #2 (3.7, $135), FTAI's retrofitted CFM56 aeroderivative #3 (3.4, $132), reciprocating gas engines #4 (3.3, $189), and industrial gas turbines #5 (1.8, $258). Weights are 50% SCACP, 15% noise/NIMBY, 15% technology maturity, and 10% each for load following and emissions.

The ranking depends on the time premium. With no time-to-power premium (2030 view), fast-start reciprocating engines and SOFCs tie at 3.8, aeroderivatives score 3.7, micro turbines 3.5, and industrial turbines 1.6. MS says the market debate is how long the acute time-to-power problem lasts.

The grid is not displaced. MS expects combined-cycle gas turbines (CCGTs) or the grid to remain the primary source for 1 GW+ training mega-sites. Modular options (fuel cells, small turbines) gain as compute moves to smaller inference nodes.

Storage is the balancing layer. MS expects hybrid setups, a fast thermal source plus batteries, to become the default onsite architecture. US energy storage (ESS) demand is forecast to grow from 57 GWh in 2025 to about 280 GWh in 2030, roughly 60% for data centers (169 GWh in 2030).

Virtual power plants (VPPs) are reaching power-plant scale. On Sept 9, 2026 Sunrun and Tesla coordinated over 140,000 home batteries to deliver more than 580 MW for a three-hour California dispatch. 517 MW came from about 110,000 Powerwalls and Sunrun owned 55% of the participating Powerwalls. A framework with Renew Home targets over 16 GW of flexible capacity for utilities and hyperscalers.

Supply/demand debate: MS counts 149 GW of primary gas-gen equipment supply by 2030, enough for 120 GW of data center power with a 20% overbuild, against about 150 GW of incremental data center demand. Its table shows a surplus of 19.9 GW/yr in 2027 and 4.8 GW/yr in 2028, then shortages of 15.1 GW/yr in 2029 and 29.2 GW/yr in 2030.

Pricing and booking evidence for suppliers: prices are rising for large-frame and industrial turbines, down payments for slot reservations are up to 25% for 2030 delivery of large-frame turbines, and INIO and CAT are fully booked through 2028 with pricing locked. 2030 is called the pivot point.

MS says BTM power is not just a bridge. A flywheel runs from data center demand to manufacturing scale, lower costs for fuel cells and microgrids, then adoption by C&I customers. MS forecasts about 10 GW of incremental US C&I demand a year through 2030, on top of the BTM TAM, and says reshoring could require as much as 113 GW of incremental capacity through 2035.

Political pushback is expected to support BTM. About $156 billion of data center projects were cancelled or delayed in 2025 and $130 billion in 1Q26. Texas is auditing more than 474 GW of ERCOT interconnection requests. Virginia moved toward 'cost causer pays' and Pennsylvania ended fast-track permitting. MS says most efforts aim to slow, not reverse, the build-out.

Physical AI extends the theme: vehicles and robots become inference nodes and, if battery-equipped, power assets. MS estimates robot/EV compute capacity could reach about 1.0 TW by 2040, which it frames as a longer-term Distributed Inference Cloud.

market_movers.rationale: Bloom Energy's SOFC ranks #1 on MS's BTM composite score at 4.5/5 on the fastest time to power (under 6 months), 800V DC output, load following and low noise and emissions. Analyst is David Arcaro.

BorgWarner's TurboCell micro turbine generator ranks #2 at 3.7/5. The report points to a corresponding BWA upgrade note. Analyst is Andrew Percoco. The ratings table, priced 10/05, still shows Equal-weight.
FTAI's retrofitted CFM56 aeroderivative genset (~25 MW) ranks #3 at 3.4/5 with a $132/MWh SCACP. Analyst is Kristine Liwag.
INNIO Jenbacher is a top idea among reciprocating gas engine makers. MS says INIO is fully booked through 2028 with pricing and shipments locked.
ERock's modular 1.5-3.5 MW gas gensets are listed among the key overweight-rated reciprocating engine names.
Cummins is listed as a key overweight-rated reciprocating gas engine supplier in the BTM equipment table.
Baker Hughes is the top idea in industrial gas turbines (NovaLT), the lowest-ranked technology at 1.8/5 with a $258/MWh SCACP. Analyst is Joe Laetsch.
Solaris is a top idea among onsite power developers. MS counts it among developers holding procured BTM equipment.
Liberty is a top idea among onsite power developers and is named among the developers that have procured BTM equipment.
Halliburton (with VoltaGrid) is a top idea among onsite power developers and is named among the developers that have procured BTM equipment.
Williams is a top idea among onsite power developers and is named among the developers that have procured BTM equipment.
Tesla is named a key energy storage and VPP provider. Its Powerwalls supplied 517 MW of the 580 MW September California dispatch.
Sunrun is a key VPP provider. It owned and operated 55% of participating Powerwalls and dispatched over 30,000 additional customer batteries.
Fluence is named a key ESS provider as data center storage demand rises toward 169 GWh in 2030.
Ford is listed among key ESS/VPP providers, without a stated thesis in this note.
Rolls Royce (mtu Series 4000 gas gensets) is named a top onsite power equipment idea. It has no US listing, so no ticker is given.

sector_views.sector: Behind-the-meter power equipment and onsite power developers
sector_views.rationale: Time-to-power constraints, rising turbine pricing, bookings locked through 2028 and a projected 2029-2030 supply shortage support demand for onsite generation.
The note carries an In-Line industry view for North America, benchmarked to the S&P 500.

trade_ideas.description: Long onsite power equipment suppliers: BE, BKR, BWA, CMI, EROC, FTAI, INIO
trade_ideas.rationale: BTM equipment is expected to fill a 77 GW data center power shortfall, with prices rising and supply tightening into 2029-2030.
trade_ideas.risk: Oversupply from new entrants by 2030, or an easing of the time-to-power constraint, which narrows the ranking gap between technologies.

trade_ideas.description: Long onsite power developers: SEI, LBRT, HAL, WMB
trade_ideas.rationale: These developers hold procured BTM generation equipment (23 GW across SEI, PUMP, WMB, LBRT and HAL/VoltaGrid) for deployment at data center sites.

trade_ideas.description: Long ESS and VPP providers: TSLA, F, FLNC, BWA, RUN
trade_ideas.rationale: Storage smooths inference-driven load spikes, and VPPs showed power-plant-scale dispatch of 580 MW in California.

risk_factors: Equipment oversupply by 2030 if new-entrant capacity materializes and time-to-power differences narrow.
Technology maturity and reliability vary across new entrants, and some capacity may be temporary bridge power.
Emissions, air quality and noise (NIMBY) scrutiny rises as nodes move closer to population centers.
Data center moratoriums and permitting limits could slow the overall build-out.
SMRs have no commercially available product and face 5-10 year timelines.
Solar plus storage is limited behind the meter by land needs and intermittency.
Composite rankings depend on subjective weights, and developers with different priorities could rank technologies differently.
Morgan Stanley discloses investment banking and other relationships with many companies named in the note.
charts_described: Exhibit 2 shows the US data center power shortfall through 2029 (midpoint) as 160.0 GW of demand, less 21.8 GW under construction, 36.2 GW of grid access, 22.8 GW of BTM backlog and 2.8 GW of nuclear siting, leaving a 76.5 GW net shortfall.
Exhibit 3 shows SCACP in $/MWh stacking BTM LCOE and a stranded compute premium. Grid power has the lowest LCOE at $89 but the highest total at $323.
Exhibit 7 shows US ESS annual demand rising from 57 GWh in 2025 to about 280 GWh in 2030, with data center ESS demand reaching 169 GWh.
Exhibit 23 shows gas-gen equipment supply minus data center demand incl. 20% overbuild at +19.9, +4.8, -15.1 and -29.2 GW/yr for 2027E-2030E.
geopolitical: Local and state opposition to data centers is growing ahead of the midterm elections, focused on power bills, water and air pollution, and noise, dust and traffic.
Texas is auditing data centers in ERCOT's interconnection queue, which holds more than 474 GW of pending requests, about 90% data center-related.
Virginia's July 31 Rider T1 order moves Dominion toward 'cost causer pays' for direct-connect transmission.
Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro issued an executive order ending fast-track permitting for data centers, requiring local approval, barring NDAs and requiring projects to bring their own capacity.
Ohio's Vivek Ramaswamy 'Ohioans-First' proposal is not current law and is read as a sentiment indicator.
Bipartisan US reshoring of manufacturing is expected to add electricity demand.

tension_points.bull_case: MS sees demand outpacing supply by 2029-2030. It counts 149 GW of supply against about 150 GW of data center demand needing a 20% overbuild. Prices and down payments are rising, and INIO and CAT are booked through 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: The industry could be oversupplied, with many players adding capacity. MS's own table shows a 19.9 GW/yr surplus in 2027 and 4.8 GW/yr in 2028 before shortages in 2029-2030.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Unlimited equipment availability by 2030 would narrow the time-to-power differential, so winners would be decided on cost and operating traits.

tension_points.bull_case: Interconnection delays of 5-7 years, rising grid prices and political pushback make onsite, modular power a durable architecture and not just a bridge.
tension_points.bear_case: The grid remains the lowest-cost source, and CCGTs or the grid are best suited to 1 GW+ mega-campuses because of economies of scale and proven technology.

theme_stances.key_argument: A growing power shortfall, political pushback and the shift to inference make behind-the-meter power a durable architectural shift.
theme_stances.evidence: Behind-the-meter (BTM) power is a structural architectural shift

theme_stances.key_argument: Storage smooths inference-driven load spikes and pairs with fast thermal generation as the default onsite setup.
theme_stances.evidence: Storage remains the balancing factor for data center power.

theme_stances.key_argument: MS argues 2030 supply is likely overstated and demand understated, so it stays bullish on the supply/demand balance.
theme_stances.evidence: Supply potentially overstated and demand understated in 2030.
